messages:
maya.k: Heads-up — last night's SCIM sync appears to have removed the `data-science` group mapping from Okta -> Redwood. I can see members lost group membership but several retained Admin role in the console.

ajay.r: Did they get deprovisioned or just unlinked from the group?

maya.k: Unlinked. SCIM job returned 200s for PATCHs, but user role removal didn't happen.

jen.s: Quick theory: we recently changed the mapping for the Okta attribute used for role entitlements (`entitlements` -> `roles`). If SCIM is looking at the old attribute it may not detect role linkage to remove.

samir.e: I pulled the SCIM event for one affected user: 
```
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "path": "groups[value eq \"abcd-1234\"]",
      "value": []
    }
  ]
}
```
Response: 200 OK, applied. No errors.

svc-scim-bot: Automated: deprovision event 1763108400 processed for group abcd-1234, members removed from group mapping. (audit_id: sync-2026-03-18-23)

ajay.r: So group membership removed (mapping succeeded) but role unassignment uses `entitlements` array which appears to be empty in the incoming payload. If people had Admin via a role assignment tied to that group, SCIM won't revoke unless we see the entitlement change.

jen.s: Can you grep the raw provisioning payloads for `entitlements`? I want to confirm whether Okta sent them and if our mapping pipeline dropped them.

samir.e: Ran this on the sync logs: `jq '.Operations[]?.value[]?.entitlements' sync-2026-03-18.log | grep -v null | wc -l` -> 0. So no entitlements in those ops.

maya.k: That matches audit: 7 users left the group but still have Admin role. I flagged them in the console and escalated.

ajay.r: Short-term remediation: run a backfill that recomputes roles from current group membership on master auth DB and revoke roles for users not in the corresponding group. I can run a controlled job that targets only the `data-science` mapping.

jen.s: Also add a rule in the SCIM processor: if a group->role mapping is removed and the incoming payload removes the group, treat that as an implicit entitlement removal even if entitlements array is absent. But that has to be careful for manual overrides.

samir.e: Agree. For immediate action: ajay, please run the backfill with dry-run first and post counts. We'll coordinate with support to notify affected users.

ajay.r: Running dry-run now: `./scripts/backfill_roles.sh --group-id abcd-1234 --dry-run`
(2m later)
ajay.r: Dry-run results: would revoke Admin from 7 accounts, keep 2 (they have direct non-group Admin grants).

maya.k: Good. Please proceed with live run after a 15-minute window. I'll prepare Slack DM template for affected folks.

svc-scim-bot: Alert created: incident-2026-03-18-193 (severity: medium) — SCIM group->role drift detected.

jen.s: Followups: 1) Add telemetry for missing entitlement attributes on incoming events, 2) Add a flag to force role reconcile on group-remove ops, 3) Ask Okta team if they changed the attribute mapping.

samir.e: Filed task: ENG-SEC-1129 (add entitlement telemetry + reconcile flag). Assigning to eng-infra.

maya.k: Thanks all. ajay, ping when live run completes and paste audit IDs. :thumbsup:

ajay.r: Live run done. Audit IDs: audit-57821 (revoke ops), audit-57822 (post-check). Revoked Admin from 7 accounts. No regressions detected in 30m monitoring.

jen.s: Closing loop with Okta - they confirmed a change last week moved entitlements to a custom attribute `x_roles` and we hadn't updated mapping. I've opened okta ticket OKTA-564. They'll add a transition alias for 7 days.

maya.k: Great. Let's keep the reconcile alert for 72h and then drop the alias once done.

samir.e: Noted. Added a short postmortem to the incidents channel.

maya.k: Thanks team.
